transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
A Russian ballistic missile attack on Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky's hometown
killed two people and injured dozens.
A Russian cargo ship caught fire in the Gulf of Finland after being hit by drones.
The big slides in A.I. shares and the broader stock market is raising concerns
about whether we are in the midst of a financial bubble that might end badly.
NPR's Rafael Naum reports.
A.I. companies such as NVIDIA have powered the stock market for years.
But a string of recent problems in the A.I. sector are raising concerns
about whether investors will see the returns they were expecting.
The fear is that we could be in the midst of a financial bubble,
similar to the dot-com era of the 1990s,
since A.I. companies have become such an essential part of financial markets
and the wider economy.
Some analysts fear it could be even worse.
A.I. companies have borrowed massive amounts of money.
And trouble in one or two companies could spark a chain reaction
that could even lead to a financial crisis.
Rafael Naum, NPR News.
A judge has ruled that the Trump administration's plan to overhaul funding
for homelessness programs is unlawful.
NPR's Jennifer Ludden reports that under President Trump,
HUD wants to shift money away from programs that support permanent housing.
The decision is the latest setback for the Trump administration's push
to fund more transitional housing with mandated treatment for addiction.
The ruling found that doing so would exceed HUD's authority
and go against requirements set by Congress.
The judge also struck down a restriction on so-called harm reduction efforts,
like offering clean needle exchanges for drug users.
Democratic-led states and homeless advocacy groups brought the suit
and argued that long-term housing without preconditions
has a long track record of success.
HUD Secretary Scott Turner disputes that claim
and told Reuters the agency reserves the right to appeal.
The court ruling comes just over a week before the deadline
when local providers must apply for federal grants.
Jennifer Ludden, NPR News, Washington.
A final draft of a climate agreement at U.N. COP 31 talks in Antalya, Turkey
has failed to mention the impact of fossil fuels on global warming,
leading international delegates to add another day to their deliberations.
NPR's Rachel Waltoltz has more from Antalya.
Many of the countries that have been most affected by climate change,
they want the agreement that comes out of Antalya to explicitly state
that it's necessary for the world to transition away from fossil fuels
and oil-producing countries, notably Saudi Arabia and Russia,
they're resisting that language.
Burning fossil fuels like coal and oil and natural gas,
it's the primary driver of climate change.
It is also the key to the global economy,
and so it's always a delicate issue.
This is NPR News in Washington.
One of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives has been captured by Mexican authorities.
Fosto Isidro Medza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro,
was wanted on drug trafficking and firearms violations.
The arrest in Sinaloa came with extensive gunfire and vehicles burned.
Mexico says that Trump administration intelligence helped.
Women are more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease than men.
NPR's Ping Wang reports that new research suggests
that changes during menopause may contribute.
In midlife, most women stop getting their periods.
The transition comes with fluctuating hormones,
which affect parts of the brain involved in memory.
Stephanie Perez, a researcher at the University of Texas at San Antonio,
says in normal aging, the brain compensates to spine.
But when you have these different genetic risk factors,
not only for Alzheimer's disease, but even for psychiatric illnesses,
when you go through the transition, you're just more at risk.
In mice, Perez and her colleagues found that a predisposition to Alzheimer's
meant more risk for cognitive decline.
They think it's related to hormonal changes
and are now looking into which ones and how they affect risks.
She says current hormone replacement therapies,
which tamp down on hot flashes,
are not universally helpful with cognitive deficits.
The research was presented at the Society for Neuroscience conference.
Ping Wang, NPR News.
As a new Democratic-controlled Congress prepares to convene within the next two months,
President Trump is bracing for inquiries with a new executive order
directing contractors who've done business with the administration
to consult with Trump's team before talking to Congress.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Russian ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown kills two and injures dozens
Russian cargo ship catches fire in Gulf of Finland after drone strikes
Rising A.I. stock slides raise fears of a financial bubble, NPR's Rafael Naum reports
Judge rules Trump administration's HUD homelessness funding overhaul unlawful, Jennifer Ludden reports
Draft COP31 climate agreement in Antalya, Turkey omits fossil fuels, adding a day of talks
FBI Ten Most Wanted fugitive Fausto Isidro Meza Flores captured in Sinaloa, Mexico
Women more likely to develop Alzheimer's; menopause changes may contribute, Ping Wang reports
Trump executive order requires contractors to consult his team before talking to Congress
